Sunita Kulkarni, a 68-year-old female, came with pain and swelling of the small joints of the hands and feet, and morning
stiffness lasting for a long time, which had been increasing over the recent past.
HISTORY
The trouble had been going on for a long time, with gradual worsening. She had taken some medicines for pain earlier, but the
symptoms kept coming back. No significant past history was reported.
ON EXAMINATION
On examination, the patient was conscious and oriented, with a fair general condition. The small joints of the hands and feet
were swollen and tender, with restricted movement. There was no deformity at the time of admission.

and medicines were given in the ward along with therapy sessions. She responded well to the treatment, with gradual
reduction in pain and swelling. She stayed for 7 days 8 hours and was discharged in a stable condition.
CONDITION AT DISCHARGE
At discharge, her joint pain and swelling had settled considerably. She was walking comfortably and taking food well. She was
afebrile and her general condition was good.
ADVICE ON DISCHARGE
She was advised to continue the medicines as prescribed, and to follow the diet and activity instructions given. She was asked
to come back for a follow-up review after a few days. She was told to return sooner if the pain or swelling increased, or if she
developed any new symptoms.

The trouble had been going on for some time, and simple measures at home had not given relief. There was no significant past
history of any long-standing illness.

mobilise and take oral feeds as tolerated.

Usha Pillai, a 64-year-old female, was brought in with pain in the hip and inability to bear weight on the affected
limb following a fall at home earlier that night.
History
The patient had sustained the injury a few hours before arrival and had not been able to stand or walk since. No
prior treatment was taken for this episode. There was no significant past history of any long-standing illness.
On Examination
On examination the patient was conscious and oriented, in painful distress, and lying supine with the affected limb
held in a position of comfort. The affected hip was tender to touch and any movement of the joint was painful and
restricted. The limb was shortened and externally rotated, and the patient was unable to lift it off the bed.
Course in Hospital
The  patient  was  admitted  and  evaluated  with  laboratory  tests  and  imaging,  which  confirmed  Displaced
intracapsular fracture of the neck of the femur. After fitness was obtained, the patient was taken up for Total hip
arthroplasty under anaesthesia, and an implant was used during the procedure. Medicines were given in the ward
in the post-operative period, and the patient was encouraged to mobilise with support as pain settled. The post-
operative period was uneventful and the patient recovered steadily.
Condition at Discharge

The patient was able to stand and walk with support and was taking food well.

and to report any discharge, redness or fever. A soft, nutritious diet and gradual walking with support were advised,
avoiding squatting, sitting cross-legged and heavy lifting. The patient was asked to return for review as scheduled,

dressings changed as advised. A soft, nutritious diet and graded walking with support are to be continued, avoiding stairs and
heavy lifting for now. Review in the outpatient department after a few days, and report sooner if there is fever, increasing pain,
discharge from the wound or difficulty in breathing.

Final diagnosis Cataract
Procedure performed Cataract surgery
PRESENTING COMPLAINTS
Harish Reddy, a 70-year-old male, came with complaints of gradual painless diminution of vision in one eye for some time,
with difficulty in seeing in bright light and while reading.
HISTORY
The trouble had been progressing over a long period. No significant past history was reported. He had been using spectacles
and topical eye drops before coming in, without relief.
ON EXAMINATION
On examination, the patient was conscious, oriented and ambulant. Ocular examination showed a cataractous lens in the
affected eye with reduced visual acuity. The anterior segment was otherwise unremarkable and the eye was not inflamed.
COURSE IN HOSPITAL
He was assessed and taken up for Cataract surgery under local anaesthesia. The procedure was completed uneventfully and an
intraocular lens implant was placed. He was given medicines in the ward and remained comfortable overnight. He was
reviewed the next morning and found fit for discharge.
CONDITION AT DISCHARGE
At discharge, the patient was comfortable, with no pain or redness in the operated eye. The wound was healthy, he was
walking without support and taking food well.
ADVICE ON DISCHARGE
He was advised to take the prescribed medicines regularly, use the eye drops as instructed and keep the eye protected. He was
told to avoid rubbing the eye, heavy lifting and exposure to dust or water, and to take a normal diet with adequate rest. He was
asked to return for review as scheduled, and to come back sooner if there was pain, redness, discharge or any fall in vision.
Dr Ishita Kapoor

Final diagnosis NS1-positive dengue fever with thrombocytopenia
Presenting Complaints
Nikhil Joshi, a 51-year-old male, was admitted on 24 August 2025 02:45 hrs with a history of high-grade fever with chills,
severe body ache and headache, and generalised weakness.
History
The fever had been ongoing for a few days before presentation, with no significant relief from the medicines taken at home.
There was no significant past history of any long-standing illness.
On Examination
On admission, the patient was conscious and oriented, though visibly unwell and lethargic. Examination of the abdomen
revealed mild tenderness in the right hypochondrium, and the skin showed a faint flushing over the trunk. The patient was
clinically stable, with no signs of bleeding or fluid accumulation.
Course in Hospital
The patient was assessed and investigated with laboratory tests, which showed a low platelet count, and the diagnosis of NS1-
positive dengue fever with thrombocytopenia was confirmed. Treatment was started with intravenous fluids, antipyretics and
supportive care, with regular monitoring of platelet counts and vital parameters. The patient responded well to the treatment,
with fever settling and platelet counts improving steadily over the course of the stay. No operation or procedure was performed
during this admission, and the patient remained in the Deluxe room throughout.
Condition at Discharge
At the time of discharge on 27 August 2025 00:45 hrs, the patient was afebrile, haemodynamically stable and ambulatory. The
appetite had returned to normal, and there was no bleeding or rash noted.
Advice on Discharge
The patient was advised to continue the prescribed oral medicines as directed, with plenty of oral fluids and a light, nutritious
diet. He was asked to avoid strenuous activity for a few days and to maintain adequate hydration. A follow-up review was
arranged, and he was instructed to report immediately if there was any recurrence of fever, bleeding from any site, or
worsening weakness.

The patient was conscious and oriented, in mild discomfort. The affected wrist was swollen and tender, with deformity and

The patient was assessed and laboratory tests and imaging were done. Closed reduction and percutaneous K-wire fixation of
the distal radius was carried out under anaesthesia and an implant was used. Medicines were given in the ward and the patient
